sam: ran a 30s nsight systems trace on the new prefetch path, attaching observations. link: https://perf/reports/1759876543 :eyes:
leah: nice, can you paste the high-level waterfall? are kernels overlapping with memcpy or getting serialized?
sam: quick notes: many small `cudaMemcpyAsync` host->device on stream 7 that appear to be blocking stream 0 kernels. timeline shows memcpy on copy engine but kernel launches mostly queued until host wakes (CPU gaps). cpu sleep spans line up with huge memcpy spikes.
sam: command used: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --cuda-memory-usage --output=1759876543 --sample=cpu```
leah: hmm, do you see prefetch doing pinned vs pageable memcpy? that would explain copy-engine fallback and host involvement.
ony: (typo) sorry meant tony
tony: not an expert but if prefetch uses `cudaMemcpy` (sync) instead of `cudaMemcpyAsync` with a pinned buffer it'll stall CPU. are we allocating from `host_pool` or fallbacking to malloc?
sam: checked heap allocations: prefetch path hits fallback to `malloc` for ~12% of requests (small batches, rare), meaning non-pinned copies. that matches the host wakeups.
leah: ok try switching the prefetch allocator to pinned pool (pinned_pool->reserve) for small-object path, or use `cudaHostRegister` early. low-risk toggle for next canary. :thumbsup:
tony: also look at kernel selection — the fast kernel variant requires a warm KV cache, but we see kvcache misses triggering a heavy prefetch flood that amplifies the problem. try reducing `max_prefetch_bytes` by 2x to spread copies.
anya: perf-bot flagged a regression on the batcher since commit `e3f2a1d` that increased prefetch aggressiveness. bot shows +18% hostcopy time on p90.
perf-bot: automated alert — regression detected: hostcopy_time_p90 increased from 34ms to 40ms after e3f2a1d. trace sample id=1759876543.
sam: plan: 1) run targeted nsight with stream names annotated (add `--capture-range=timerange` around batcher prefetch), 2) flip to pinned_pool for prefetch path, 3) run microbench with `max_prefetch_bytes=0.5x` to see effect on overlap.
leah: for the nsight capture, also enable `--os-threads` to see CPU scheduling gaps. look for repeated sleep->wakeup aligned to memcpy start.
tony: small note — kernel selection may be mis-picking the high-sharedmem kernel when batch size is 1. add a heuristic: require kvcache_hits >= 2 before selecting that kernel. reduces cold-start tail.
sam: ran a quick iteration: pinned_pool flip dropped hostcopy p90 to 28ms in a synthetic run, and CPU wakeups reduced. nvtx markers show memcpy on copy engine overlapped with kernel more often.
leah: awesome, can you push that as a warm-up toggle behind a feature flag? we can roll back if we see allocator pressure.
sam: yep. I'll open a PR referencing trace id and attach the nsight timeline screenshot. will also run a 1hr canary to validate end-to-end. ETA ~ today EOD. :clock3:
anya: please also capture `/proc/sched_debug` and `dmesg` on canary hosts, just in case prefetch floods push CPU into deeper sleep states.
sam: noted. I'll include kernel lists and nvprof hotspots too (mostly `prefetch_copy_kernel` and `kv_lookup`).
leah: thanks — TL;DR: hostcopy vs kernel serialization caused by pageable fallbacks + aggressive prefetch. quick wins: pinned pool + reduce prefetch budget + kernel-selection guard.
sam: filing follow-up with artifacts: nsight full trace, nvprof hotspots, pinned_pool benchmark. thread will be updated when canary completes.
leah: :rocket:
